Ground-dwelling civet. Good indicator of forest floor integrity.

sensitivity_to_disturbance: Low - highly adaptable to modified habitats
notes: Arboreal civet, so camera trap detection is lower than actual abundance. Very adaptable.

seasonal_variation: Higher during wet season when flooded habitat expands.
notes: Indicator species for wetland health. Highest at mangrove and riparian stations.

sensitivity_to_disturbance: Very high - avoids construction noise, night lighting, and road traffic
seasonal_variation: Movement patterns shift with food availability. May move to coastal areas during dry spells.
population_estimate_johor: 150-200 individuals statewide (2024 Perhilitan aerial survey). Small ranging group (~8-12) uses Tanjung Balau-Panti corridor.
notes: Johor had 253 human-elephant conflict cases in 2024. Elephants at Desaru use a narrow corridor between Panti Forest Reserve and coastal forest. Any development that blocks this corridor causes immediate displacement. Construction noise alone (>60dB) triggers avoidance within 1-2km radius.

sensitivity_to_disturbance: Moderate (habitat) but extremely vulnerable to targeted poaching
seasonal_variation: Minimal natural variation. Solitary and cryptic.
population_estimate_johor: Unknown - Critically Endangered, populations depleted across range
notes: World's most trafficked mammal. Malaysian populations under intense pressure from organized trafficking networks supplying Chinese and Vietnamese traditional medicine markets. Decline pattern across multiple stations simultaneously is signature of systematic poaching (versus localized habitat disturbance which affects single stations). Even 1-2 detections/month represents meaningful population at a site.
